title: Experiences, Travel & Present Perfect
subtitle: Talk about life experiences and choose Present Perfect or Past Simple accurately.

units.title: Travel & Life Experiences
units.tagline: Ask about experiences with ever and never.
notes: Use Present Perfect for an experience when the exact past time is not important: I have visited a mountain village.
Make questions with Have/Has + subject + past participle: Have you ever travelled by boat?
Use never for an experience that has not happened: I have never slept in a tent.
Travel vocabulary can make experience questions more specific: destination, journey, guide, village and coast.

vocabulary.meaning: the place a person is travelling to
vocabulary.example: The island was their final destination.

vocabulary.meaning: an act of travelling from one place to another
vocabulary.example: The train journey took three hours.

vocabulary.meaning: a person who shows visitors around a place
vocabulary.example: A guide explained the history of the town.
The village had an unusual bridge.
The student invented a simple water filter.

grammar.title: Present Perfect for experience
grammar.rule: Present Perfect: have/has + past participle. Belirsiz bir geçmiş deneyimden söz ederken kullanılır. Zamanı belirtmeyiz; deneyimin şu anla bağlantısı vardır.
examples: I have visited a coastal town.

grammar.title: Ever and never
grammar.rule: Ever genellikle soru cümlelerinde 'hayatında hiç' anlamı verir. Never olumsuz bir anlam taşır; bu yüzden ayrıca don't kullanmayız.
examples: Have you ever seen a volcano?
I have never flown in a small plane.
He has never visited that museum.

units.remember: have/has + üçüncü hâl: I have been, she has gone, we have seen. Düzensiz fiillerin 1/2/3 hâllerini birlikte tekrar et.
units.watchOut: 'I have never been...' zaten olumsuzdur; 'I haven't never been...' çift olumsuz olur.

practice.prompt: Have you ever ___ to another city by train?
practice.hint: After have, use the past participle.

practice.prompt: Choose the correct Present Perfect question.
options: Have you ever visited a cave?
Did you ever visited a cave?
Have you ever visit a cave?

practice.prompt: They have ___ an unusual place near the coast.
Which word means a place you are travelling to?
I have never ___ in a tent.
A person who shows visitors around is a ___.

reading.title: The Windmill Project
reading.text: Arda lives in a small village where the dry season can be difficult. He has always enjoyed finding practical solutions. Last year, he read about wind power and started to build a small windmill with old bicycle parts. He has learned a lot from the project, although the first version did not work well. This month, the windmill has helped charge a small battery for the village library. Arda has not become famous, but he has shown that a creative idea can begin with simple materials.

questions.prompt: What did Arda use for the windmill?
What has the windmill helped do this month?
What idea does the text show?
options: A simple idea can grow into something useful.
Creative projects need only expensive materials.
A village cannot use wind power.

listening.title: An Unusual Destination
listening.script: Seda: Have you ever visited a place that was completely different from your town? Karim: Yes, I have. Two years ago, I went to a village near a salt lake. The ground looked white, and the water changed colour in the evening. Seda: Have you ever travelled with a guide? Karim: No, I haven't. My cousin knew the area, so she showed us the best places. Seda: I have never seen a salt lake, but I would like to go.

questions.prompt: Where did Karim go two years ago?
options: To a village near a salt lake

questions.prompt: What changed colour in the evening?
Who showed Karim the best places?

units.title: Present Perfect or Past Simple?
units.tagline: Move to Past Simple when a specific finished time is given.
notes: Use Present Perfect for a general experience: Have you ever seen a desert?
Use Past Simple when the conversation gives a specific, finished time: Yes, I saw one last summer.
A follow-up question with When? asks for that specific past time, so Past Simple follows.
Verb forms matter: see → saw → seen; go → went → gone; write → wrote → written.

grammar.title: Specific past time
grammar.rule: Yesterday, last summer, in 2024 gibi bitmiş ve belirli zaman ifadeleriyle Past Simple kullanılır. Present Perfect ile bu tür zaman ifadelerini birlikte kullanma.

grammar.title: The follow-up pattern
grammar.rule: Önce deneyimi sor: Have you ever ...? Cevaptan sonra zamanı sor: When did you ...? İlk soru Present Perfect, zaman sorusu ve cevabı Past Simple olur.

units.remember: Hayat deneyimi = Present Perfect. Zamanı bitmiş ve açıkça belirtilmiş olay = Past Simple.
units.watchOut: 'I have visited Rome last year' yanlış. 'I visited Rome last year' doğru; zaman belirtilmiyorsa 'I have visited Rome' kullanılabilir.

practice.prompt: Have you ever ___ a famous building?
She has never ___ a song in public.

Choose the sentence about a general experience.
options: I have tried climbing last Friday.

practice.prompt: Which time expression signals Past Simple here?

reading.title: A Journey to the Cliff Village
reading.text: Nora has always wanted to visit the cliff village of Varda. Last spring, she travelled there with her uncle. They took a bus to the coast and then walked along a narrow path. Nora has taken many photographs of the houses built into the rock, but her favourite moment happened on the second day. A local guide told them how people carried water to the village before there was a road. Since that journey, Nora has read more about unusual places and has started a small travel notebook.

questions.prompt: When did Nora travel to Varda?
What has Nora taken many of?
What has Nora started since the journey?

speaking.title: Experience Interview
speaking.prompt: Ask and answer three experience questions. After each yes answer, ask one Past Simple follow-up question with When, Where or Who.
support: I ... last year / in July / with my family.

writing.title: A Place I Have Visited
writing.prompt: Write 8–10 sentences about a place you have visited, or an unusual place you would like to visit. Use two Present Perfect sentences for experiences and two Past Simple sentences with a finished time.
support: I would like to visit ... because ...

finalQuiz.prompt: Which word is common in Present Perfect experience questions?

options: I visited a cave in May.
